elements.element: Vendor assigns to Customer all right, title, and interest in Deliverables created for Customer.
elements.evidence: Section 14.2 instead provides that Vendor exclusively owns every Deliverable; no assignment to Customer appears.

elements.element: Vendor assigns to Customer all right, title, and interest in other work product created for Customer.
elements.evidence: The clause contains no ownership allocation or assignment covering work product beyond Deliverables.

elements.element: Vendor retains ownership of its pre-existing IP.
elements.evidence: Section 14.3 states that Vendor retains Vendor Technology, and the added language confirms Vendor ownership of its generic tools and know-how.

elements.element: Customer receives a licence to Vendor IP embedded in or required to use the Deliverables.
elements.evidence: Section 14.3 applies the Section 13.2 licence to Vendor Technology incorporated in or required to use a Deliverable.

elements.element: The licence to embedded Vendor IP is perpetual.
elements.evidence: Section 14.3 expressly describes the applicable Section 13.2 licence as perpetual.

elements.element: The licence to embedded Vendor IP is irrevocable.
elements.evidence: Section 14.3 does not make the separate licence to embedded Vendor Technology irrevocable. The added irrevocability language addresses the licence to each Deliverable and also conflicts with Section 14.2's revocability language.

elements.element: The licence to embedded Vendor IP is royalty-free.
elements.evidence: Section 14.3 does not state that the separate licence to embedded Vendor Technology is royalty-free.

elements.element: Customer retains all rights in Customer Data.

elements.evidence: The clause uses exclusive ownership for Deliverables and retains Vendor Technology and generic tools and know-how for Vendor; it creates no joint ownership.
The added language expressly states that Vendor owns its generic tools.
The added language expressly states that Vendor owns its know-how.

elements.element: Customer receives a licence to each Deliverable.
elements.evidence: Section 14.2 grants Customer a licence to use each Deliverable, and the added language confirms Customer's licence to each Deliverable.

elements.element: Customer's licence to each Deliverable is perpetual.
elements.evidence: Although the added sentence calls the licence perpetual, Section 14.2 still limits it to the applicable Order Form term. The attempted disapplication refers to the 'preceding sentence,' which is the generic-tools-and-know-how sentence, not Section 14.2's limitation.

elements.element: Customer's licence to each Deliverable is irrevocable.
elements.evidence: The clause simultaneously calls the licence revocable and irrevocable. The attempted disapplication does not operatively point to the Section 14.2 sentence containing the revocability limitation.

elements.element: Customer's licence to each Deliverable is worldwide.
elements.evidence: The added language expressly makes the licence worldwide, with no contrary territorial limitation.

elements.element: Customer's licence to each Deliverable is royalty-free.
elements.evidence: The added language expressly makes the licence royalty-free.

elements.element: Customer may use each Deliverable for its business.
elements.evidence: The added language expressly permits Customer to use each Deliverable for its business.

elements.element: Customer may modify each Deliverable for its business.
elements.evidence: The added language expressly permits Customer to modify each Deliverable for its business.

elements.element: Customer may sublicense each Deliverable for its business.
elements.evidence: The added language expressly permits Customer to sublicense each Deliverable for its business. A non-transferable licence does not necessarily prohibit an expressly granted sublicensing right.

result.reason: The operative text does not achieve Customer ownership or address Customer Data. It also fails the complete fallback because the new provision was placed after a generic-tools sentence, causing 'the preceding sentence' to identify the wrong sentence. Consequently, the original revocable, Order-Form-term licence remains in direct conflict with the new irrevocable, perpetual licence. The margin comment cannot cure that operative defect. The amendment otherwise states most fallback licence attributes clearly and adds no materially unrelated commercial requirement.
